dedupe_keys.name: brace for impact space weather mitigation decisions of power satellite and aviation operators during the 2024 solar maximum

description: This case study reviews what critical infrastructure operators actually did to mitigate space weather during the 2024 solar maximum, including the May 2024 Gannon storm, the largest in 20 years, which produced aurora down to 35 degrees latitude. Caitlin LaNeve, Edward Oughton and co-authors posted it on arXiv in December 2025 because few studies evaluate the mitigation strategies in use. It combines a systematic review of mitigation options for electricity transmission, satellite constellations and aviation with an anonymous survey of 303 operators (50 power, 227 satellite, 26 aviation; 55 responses) and 33 qualitative interviews. The review found 91 potential mitigation actions, and operators reported 149 actions enacted because of forecasts or experienced impacts. Coverage is international, by sector. Format and access: an open preprint with PDF. Licence: arXiv distribution licence; free to read. Caveats: an 18 percent response rate and self-reported, anonymised answers. It supports emergency response and resilience planning for operations during geomagnetic storms. Related catalogue records are the Starlink February 2022 storm loss and the Space Weather Prediction Testbed 2026 exercise.
